newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended slightly weaker, with the long-end of the curve dragged down by a weaker peseta, which eased on profit-taking.
"There's no clear explanation for today's peseta fall apart possible profit-taking," a dealer said. But he added he expected peseta strength to reemerge soon.
As evidence, he noted yield curve was steepening.
"We saw the shorter end react better than the longer one, which means people expect further official rate cuts," he said.
The peseta was trading at the close around 83.76/78 versus the mark, after touching a high of 83.42 earlier.

Early comments by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke pushed the dollar back versus the mark. He said the mark could not continue to depreciate against the dollar at the pace seen in the last few days.
On Thursday, at its regular repurchase auction, the Bank of Spain is not expected to move the key money market rate from the current six percent level, a Reuter poll showed on Wednesday.
There are also no changes expected from the Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday.
"It was a good day to take short-term profits," a dealer in Madrid added.
The 10-year cash spread over Bunds widened to 90 basis points, after having reached a record around 83 basis points this morning.
But in the shorter end, the yield curve steepened, with the differential between the two- and ten-year bond around 143 basis points from 131.
The 9.4 April 1999 ended at 108.67, with a yield near 5.20 from 5.26 percent the day before.
